lines.japanese: 自分が普通だってことに気付いたのは、最近の話だ。
lines.english: It was only recently that I realized I was ordinary.

lines.japanese: 何をもって普通と呼ぶかは様々だけど、少なくとも僕は、おとぎ話のような世界へ飛んで正義の剣をふるう救国の騎士なんかじゃなかった。
lines.english: What counts as ordinary varies from person to person. At the very least, though, I was no knight of salvation who could fly off to a fairy-tale world and wield the sword of justice.

lines.japanese: 国中から勝ちえた賞賛も、麗しの姫君と育んだ恋も、すべては出来過ぎた幻想だった。
lines.english: The praise I'd won from an entire nation, the love I'd nurtured with a beautiful princess—all of it had been a fantasy too perfect to be true.

lines.japanese: だから僕は、いまこうしてまた君と見えている不思議に、少しばかり戸惑っているんだ──
lines.english: So I'm a little bewildered to find myself here with you again—

lines.japanese: ──なんて、そんな言い方をしたら失礼かな。
lines.english: —though I suppose it would be rude to put it that way.

lines.japanese: こんにちは、誰かさん。夢の続きへようこそ。
lines.english: Hello, whoever you are. Welcome to where the dream left off.

lines.japanese: 僕の名前は羽田鷹志。私立美空学園の三年生。覚えていてくれたなら嬉しいけれど。
lines.english: My name is Takashi Haneda. I'm a third-year at Misora Private Academy. I'd be glad if you remembered me.

lines.japanese: 君と最後に会ったのはいつだったろう。まだそれほど日は経っていないはずだ。
lines.english: When was it that I last saw you? It can't have been very long ago.

lines.japanese: あれはたしか、僕のグレタガルドが終わった日、そして──
lines.english: It was, if I remember right, the day my Gretagard came to an end. And then—

lines.japanese: ──僕と渡来さんが初めて心を通わせた、その明くる朝。
lines.english: —the morning after Watarai and I first opened our hearts to each other.

lines.japanese: そう、僕と渡来さんが初めて並んで登校したあの朝だ。
lines.english: Yes. That morning when Watarai and I first walked to school together.

lines.japanese: あれから一週間ほどが経って、そばにはいつも渡来さんがいるという栄誉が、いまではもう僕の日常となり始めている。
lines.english: About a week has passed since then, and the privilege of always having Watarai beside me is already beginning to feel like part of everyday life.

lines.japanese: すぐに受けいれて、すぐに慣れて、すぐに鈍くなってしまうことは、渡来さんからも日々指摘されている僕の悪い癖だ。
lines.english: I accept things at once, grow accustomed to them at once, and at once become numb to them. It's a bad habit of mine that Watarai points out every day.
So every once in a while—

lines.japanese: ──たとえば眠れない夜には、幸福が惰性に呑まれてその色をくすませないよう、彼女のくれた笑顔や優しさや微笑ましい意地悪や、その他もろもろを思いおこすようにしている。
lines.english: —on a sleepless night, say, I make a point of remembering the smiles she's given me, her kindness, her endearing little bits of teasing, and everything else, so that happiness won't be swallowed by routine and lose its color.

lines.japanese: そうだ、丁度いいかもしれない。
lines.english: Actually, this may be the perfect opportunity.

lines.japanese: もし君が、僕の現在に興味を持って戻ってきてくれたというなら、その話を伝えよう。
lines.english: If you came back because you were curious about my life now, then I'll tell you about it.

lines.japanese: 彼女がときおり覗かせる女の子らしい茶目っ気は、当人の不興を買うから決して口外できないのだけど、僕の鏡像とも言える君になら憚る必要もないだろう。
lines.english: The girlish playfulness she lets slip from time to time is never something I could tell anyone about—she'd be displeased with me—but with you, who might be called my mirror image, I have no need to hold back.

lines.japanese: 僕と彼女の幸せな物語は、いまでもささやかに続いているんだ。
lines.english: Our quiet little happy story is still going on, even now.
